title: Two morphisms of coverings over the same morphism induce the same map on zeroth Cech sets
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $\mathcal F$ a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$. Let $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ and $\mathcal V=\{\rho_j:V_j\to V\}_{j\in J}$ be coverings, and let $f=(\chi,\alpha,(f_i)_{i\in I})$ and $g=(\chi,\beta,(g_i)_{i\in I})$ be two morphisms of coverings $\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$ lying over the same morphism $\chi:U\to V$ (so $f_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}$, $g_i:U_i\to V_{\beta(i)}$, $\rho_{\alpha(i)}f_i=\rho_{\beta(i)}g_i=\chi\circ(U_i\to U)$), with induced maps $f^*,g^*:H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)\to H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, $(f^*s)_i=\mathcal F(f_i)(s_{\alpha(i)})$, $(g^*s)_i=\mathcal F(g_i)(s_{\beta(i)})$, as in [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (a), (b). Then $f^*=g^*$. In particular, if $\mathcal U$ and $\mathcal V$ are coverings of the same object, every morphism of coverings $\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$ over the identity induces the same map $H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)\to H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$.

source.place: Sites, Lemma 00W7 (lemma-independent-refinement) and its proof; Remark 00W8 (remark-both-refine-same-H0)
